A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wikipedia/LLM study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Wikipedia data analyses, LLM rewriting simulations, machine-translation evaluations and Wikinews-based RAG experiments, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports revised impact estimates, multilingual page-view analyses, BERTScore evaluations and additional RAG model comparisons.

M1.justification: The central impact-estimation procedure changes. v1 uses a 2020–2021 frequency baseline and threshold sweeps; v2 uses a 2018–2020 baseline, selects vocabulary thresholds through intersecting rankings by pre-LLM regression R² and absolute slope, and subtracts the extrapolated 2018–2022 trend. These are substantive procedural changes despite retaining Equations 1–2.

E1.justification: Page-view coverage expands to German, Spanish and French Featured Articles, representing additional readership populations (v2 Table 3). The earlier Simple-English page-view series is absent, although Simple Articles remain in linguistic comparisons. The eight subject categories, translation languages and Wikinews question-answering task are otherwise retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-V3 as an answering model in the RAG comparisons (Tables 14–15) and Gemini 3 Pro as an alternative context rewriter (Table 10). The translation comparator set remains Facebook-NLLB, Helsinki-NLP and Google-T5.

E3.justification: Wikipedia snapshots expand from 2020–2025 to 2018–2025, and category sample counts change, including CS from 59,097 to 55,121 pages. Page views change from 30-day-normalized monthly series to seven-day-smoothed daily series extending through November 2025. Translation adds BERTScore, while the alternative RAG protocol awarding 0.25 to null outputs is removed.

E4.justification: The calibration sensitivity analyses are substantially revised: v2 adds explicit TOPK=250 versus 300 comparisons but removes the Simple-Articles-based calibration variants. It also checks translation conclusions using BERTScore and rewriting effects using Gemini 3. The four null-output scoring sensitivity tables disappear. The existing RAG case studies are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v2 introduces regression-based statistical adjustment and R²/slope-based estimator selection (Section 4.1 and Appendix B). Uncertainty reporting otherwise remains unchanged: both versions already display impact-estimate error bars without defining their statistical meaning, and neither reports seeds, repeated-run counts or significance tests.

E6.justification: Impact estimates are replaced under revised calibration, changing the headline from approximately 1–2% to approximately 1%; Table 1 also revises long-word and pronoun trends. New results cover multilingual page views, BERTScore, DeepSeek-V3 and Gemini 3. For 2024 GPT-generated questions, v2 Table 10 reports full-context accuracy of 90.42% with Gemini 3 rewriting versus 88.75% with Gemini 1.5. Existing GPT RAG scores are retained, while the 0.25-null result tables are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B introduces formal definitions of the parameter search space, candidate vocabulary and intersected parameter selection (Equations 3–5), together with the pre-LLM linear-trend model. The original estimator equations remain, and no theorems or proofs are added. The newly printed readability formulas explain existing metrics.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly presents the work as a long-term monitoring framework, adds multilingual readership decline to the introductory findings, and lowers the headline impact estimate to approximately 1%. The central contributions and claims about limited current influence, translation-evaluation distortion and possible RAG degradation remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning correlational attribution and the absence of field studies of human–LLM editing, replacing the earlier text-extraction limitation. It interprets Gemini 3 results as evidence that newer rewriters may mitigate information loss and expands the explanation of relational distortion in the Macron example. These changes materially qualify the interpretation and applicability of the findings.

D1.justification: v2 documents exact prompts for translation, article generation, news revision and the three answering settings, identifies bert-base-uncased, and supplies calibration selections and parameters for the added models. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, earlier explanations of moderation failures and discarded null translations disappear. The code/data release statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted literature on Wikipedia engagement, linguistic differences, readability, generated-data feedback and evaluation metrics, including Lyu, Herbold, Georgiou, Reinhart and BERTScore. It removes the broader Wikipedia-value paragraph and associated references. The principal novelty positioning remains; publication updates to retained Geng papers are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The direct-impact narrative is reordered from page views first to word frequency, linguistic style and then page views. Appendices are regrouped by analysis, consolidating RAG material previously split across sections. Existing introductions, experimental explanations, case interpretation, conclusion and limitations receive extensive rewriting, beyond additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column journal format and redraws the overview diagram. Translation tables become annotated bar charts, word-frequency panels are combined, and linguistic time-series plots adopt relative-value axes. New multilingual plots, BERTScore tables and prompt displays accompany extensive figure and table relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses pre-existing language drift through explicit pre-LLM calibration and sensitivity checks, makes simulations more reproducible, and states clearer causal and field-study limitations. These provide a supported quality gain. Its extent is limited by removed calibration/null-output checks, undefined error bars and incomplete integration of new evidence: DeepSeek-V3 scores 82.08% with direct answering but 75.42% with RAG on 2024 GPT-generated questions (Table 14), qualifying the broad RAG-benefit discussion.
